caption: A teammate deletes nsg-cra-prod-web directly in the Azure Portal on a Friday afternoon.

code:
Error: updating Subnet "snet-cra-prod-0"
(Virtual Network "vnet-cra-prod" /
 Resource Group "rg-cra-prod-network"):

network.SubnetsClient#CreateOrUpdate:
... NetworkSecurityGroupNotFound:
Resource ... "nsg-cra-prod-web" ...
could not be found.
caption: Thrown against the subnet association, not plainly against the missing NSG -- hence the confusion.

steps.label: 1. terraform state pull
steps.sub: Back up the current state before touching anything

steps.label: 2. terraform state list
steps.sub: See exactly what Terraform believes it manages

steps.label: 3. Decide
steps.sub: Stale entry with nothing replacing it, or already recreated by hand?

code:
# Path A -- nothing replaced it
terraform state rm azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association.prod_web
terraform state rm azurerm_network_security_group.prod_web

# Path B -- someone recreated it by hand
terraform import azurerm_network_security_group.prod_web \
  /subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/rg-cra-prod-network/providers/Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/nsg-cra-prod-web
caption: state rm edits only Terraform's bookkeeping; import adopts a real object instead of recreating it.
